standard_prerequisites.name: The ring of global sections of a proper geometrically reduced scheme is a finite separable algebra
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, the lemma on global sections of proper geometrically reduced schemes, and the lemma identifying the base change to the ring of global sections
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the spectrum of the ring of global sections is smooth and projective, so that the statement makes sense, and allows reducing to a connected scheme.

standard_prerequisites.name: Injectivity of the pullback to a closed point and equality of the classes of closed points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma on injectivity of the map to the cohomology of a point and the lemma identifying the classes of points of the same degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the implication from the second condition to the first, and the equality of the pullbacks used in the reverse implication.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of the degree zero part under base change of the field of global sections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma comparing the cohomology of the base change with the tensor product over the degree zero cohomology of the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows replacing the field of global sections by a finite separable extension so that the chosen points become rational.

core_obligations: Set up and reduce to the connected case (proof lines 3862-3876): the ring of global sections is a finite separable algebra over the base field, so its spectrum is smooth and projective; compatibility of the theory with disjoint unions reduces the statement to a connected source, which is then irreducible with field of global sections a finite separable field extension.

First equivalence (proof lines 3876-3882): the closed points appearing in the third condition may be chosen with separable residue fields, and the axioms relating pullbacks and pushforwards show that the first and the third conditions are equivalent.

Second implication (proof lines 3882-3890): if the comparison map from the cohomology of the spectrum of the ring of global sections is an isomorphism, then pulling back to any closed point with separable residue field is injective, so the first condition holds.

Remaining implication and separability (proof lines 3890-3926): assuming the first and third conditions, one extends scalars along a finite separable extension of the field of global sections, which by the base change comparison makes the chosen points rational; then the classes of the chosen points are all equal, so by the axioms the pullbacks to their cohomologies all agree, which shows that the comparison map is an isomorphism; separability of the degree zero cohomology follows from the computation for zero dimensional schemes.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an irreducible source with field of global sections.
Show the first and third conditions are equivalent through the axioms.
Use a finite separable extension making the points rational to close the equivalence and get separability.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes, for a smooth projective scheme over a base field of characteristic zero with the given data and axioms, when the comparison map from the cohomology of the spectrum of the ring of global sections to the degree zero cohomology is an isomorphism, in terms of injectivity of the pullbacks to finitely many closed points with separable residue fields, and identifies these with the generation of the top cohomology by classes of points when the scheme is equidimensional (statement lines 3859-3874). The proof (proof lines 3875-3926) reduces to the connected case, compares the conditions through the axioms, and uses a finite separable base change to make the points rational. H3: a multi step equivalence with a base change argument, written out in full.
